datasets.title: Palestine - Geodata of Damage Assessment in Gaza City, Gaza Strip - Occupied Palestinian Territory
datasets.description: This map illustrates satellite-detected damage and destruction in central Gaza City, Gaza Strip, resulting from ongoing violence in the area. Using a satellite image collected 25 July 2014 by the Pleiades satellite, and compared with a pre-crisis Pleiades image collected 6 July 2014, UNOSAT analysis has identified 133 destroyed structures, 179 severely damaged structures, and 218 moderately damaged structures. In addition, 126 craters on roads and in agricultural and non-urbanized areas are also visible as of 25 July 2014. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR/UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-damage-assessment-in-gaza-city-gaza-strip-occupied-palestinian-ter-july-31-2014]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared pre-crisis and post-crisis Pleiades satellite imagery collected on 6 July 2014 and 25 July 2014 respectively to identify and classify damage to buildings and infrastructure in Gaza City. Damage was categorized into three severity levels (destroyed, severely damaged, moderately damaged) for structures and counted as craters for roads and non-urbanized areas. Results were compiled into spatial vector datasets with damage classification attributes.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite imagery analysis using Pleiades satellite images from 6 July 2014 (pre-crisis) and 25 July 2014 (post-crisis) to detect and classify damage to structures and infrastructure through comparative image analysis.
